newsitem.title: USA: Too early to think of industry rebound - Phil Fed.
newsitem.headline: Too early to think of industry rebound - Phil Fed.

text.p: Industrial activity rose in July in the third U.S. economic district, but it is still too early to say the jump suggests the region's manufacturing sector is truly accelerating, said an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.

"There is reason to be cautious in any survey readings that we get through the summer months because of this complication of traditional closings," Michael Trebing, a Philadelphia Fed economist, told reporters on Thursday.
"I think it's too early to say this is a true acceleration in the manufacturing sector, at least in our district," the Philadelphia Fed economist added.
Trebing's remarks followed the release of the Philadelphia Fed's business activity index, which rose to 28.1 in July against 25.2 in June.

Trebing also said a rise in the price components of the Philadelphia Fed's July business survey was not a concerning signal. Commenting on the numbers, the economist said "It's not a concerning signal, to me at least."
The prices paid index of the survey rose to 19.6 in July against 15.0 in June. The prices received item was at 4.8 in July against 3.1 in the previous month.
The Philadelphia Fed covers the third U.S. economic region, which includes Delaware, the eastern region of Pennsylvania and the southern portion of New Jersey.
